title: The Information Abundance Paradox: Long Context Can Undermine What a Model Knows
hook: If the answer is always in the context window, the model stops bothering to learn it. Past an intermediate context length, more training context makes a model weaker without its crutch.
key_points: Proposes the Information Abundance Paradox: abundant in-context evidence reduces the incentive to encode that knowledge in the weights.
In pretraining, growing the context window helps language modeling, NLU, and closed-book MCQA only up to an intermediate optimum — then performance declines.
In supervised fine-tuning, more task-relevant train-time context helps when context is present but hurts robustness when it is absent or misleading.
Mechanism: informative context shifts gradient pressure away from feed-forward layers (linked to parametric knowledge) toward attention modules.
Causal interventions confirm the shift increases reliance on context at inference — so scaling toward near-infinite context is not free.
content_html: Everyone assumes longer training contexts can only help: more evidence in view, more to learn from. Arda Uzunoglu, Benjamin van Durme, and Daniel Khashabi (arXiv, August 2026) argue the opposite can happen. Their Information Abundance Paradox says that when the context already contains the answer, the model has little reason to bake that knowledge into its weights — it learns to look things up instead of learning them.
extra_html:
What they measured

In pretraining on long documents, widening the context window improves language modeling, natural language understanding, and closed-book multiple-choice QA only up to an intermediate optimum; past that point, performance consistently declines. In supervised fine-tuning, giving the model more task-relevant context at train time helps when supporting context is available at test time — but makes it markedly less robust when the context is missing or misleading.

Why it happens

The authors' analysis suggests longer context simply offers a lower-complexity solution to the training objective. Mechanistically, training with informative context shifts gradient pressure from feed-forward networks — often linked to parametric knowledge storage — toward attention modules, and causal interventions show this shift increases context reliance at inference. The practical takeaway: scaling toward near-infinite context isn't just a matter of supplying more high-quality long data. There's a trade to manage between what a model knows and what it merely retrieves.

related.title: Ring Attention for Near-Infinite Context
related.hook: Spread one long sequence across many devices and compute attention blockwise - the context length you can handle grows with the number of devices, all with exact attention and no extra overhead.

related.title: Extending Context Windows via Positional Interpolation
related.hook: Don't extrapolate to positions the model never saw - squeeze the position indices back inside the trained range, and a short fine-tune stretches the context window many times over.

related.title: WILDTRACE: Benchmarking Natural Evidence Trails in Long-Context Reasoning
related.hook: Most long-context tests plant a fake 'needle' in a haystack. Real evidence doesn't look like that — passing needle tests may not mean a model can truly reason over a document.

flashcards.prompt: What is the Information Abundance Paradox?
flashcards.back_html: When relevant information is abundant in the training context, the model has less incentive to store it in its weights — so it internalizes less and leans harder on context at inference time.

flashcards.prompt: What happens to closed-book performance as the pretraining context window keeps growing?

choices.text: It improves up to an intermediate context length, then consistently declines
It improves monotonically, since the model sees richer evidence
It is unaffected, because closed-book tasks use no context

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper finds an intermediate optimum: language modeling, NLU, and closed-book MCQA all improve at first, then degrade as context keeps growing.

flashcards.prompt: Mechanistically, where does the gradient pressure go when training with lots of informative context?
flashcards.back_html: Away from the feed-forward networks often associated with parametric knowledge, and toward the attention modules — a shift causal interventions link to greater context reliance.
